_readme: A10 (the DEMO half) — THE `chrome` APP IS BORN INSTALLED, PLACED **AND FILLED IN**.
★★ THE ACHIEVEMENT IS THE THIRD VERB, and the achado that produced this file is about usability, not
about apps: «eu instalei, apareceu os blocos lá no compose, mas eu não sei bem pra onde arrastar» — said
by the person who DESIGNED the product. A lojista would not have had a chance. ⇒ AN APP INSTALLED AND
EMPTY TEACHES LESS THAN NO APP AT ALL, because it adds five things to drag and no example of where they
go. The demo is also a living tutorial, so it has to show the finished state.
⚠️ MEASURED 2026-09-04 ON THE BENCH, and every number here is why the file exists:
· `chrome` was installed in BOTH tenants — by HAND, at 19:14 and 20:39, while somebody was testing.
Nothing in any seed installs it, and it is not in the platform seeder's list either.
· the shoe tenant carried SEVEN placements, all with test content (`"back":"a"`, `"seal":"c"`,
`"title":"2"`), and the coffee tenant carried ZERO. So the café's checkout and account screens wear
the REFERENCE mark today — our wordmark, in somebody else's shop, which is the exact outcome the app
exists to remove.
· installing it places NOTHING: the manifest declares `hooks: []`, so `seedDefaultPlacements` returns
immediately (packages/core/src/commands/extension.ts). Composing is not installing, and installing is
not placing. All three gestures are this file's.
★ THE FIVE BLOCKS AND THE FIVE SLOTS, read off the app's own manifest and confirmed against the
`target_override` column of the placements a human made on the bench:
checkout_header → storefront:checkout.header      account_header → storefront:account.header
checkout_footer → storefront:checkout.footer      account_footer → storefront:account.footer
brand           → storefront:header.brand
⛔ NOTHING WRITTEN ⇒ NOTHING DRAWN, and that is the app's decision, not a bug to work around. Every field
is optional and there is NO default word anywhere in it — a word nobody wrote would be this app choosing
Portuguese for somebody else's shop. So an unfilled block is an invisible one, which is precisely why a
demo that placed the blocks and left them empty would look like the app does nothing.
⚠️ `brand` REPLACES THE THEME'S WORDMARK rather than standing beside it (the kit's header cedes the mark
when something is placed in that slot). So a `brand` block with an empty config would DELETE the mark
from every page of the shop. Each entry below therefore carries either a logo or a word — never neither.
★★ pk19/D1 — THE WORDS THEMSELVES, REWRITTEN TO THE OWNER'S DICTATION (07/09). Everything above is about
the app being born placed; this pass is about what it SAYS. Four instructions, verbatim: the checkout
footer carries the payment methods on the left and a security line on the right; the account footer carries
a phone on the left and a contact e-mail in the middle; the account header says CARRINHO in the two shoe
stores and stays SACOLA in the café; and the checkout header is logo + step on the left with the way back
on the right.
⛔ AND THE EMPTIED FIELD IS DECLARED EMPTY, NEVER OMITTED. `planChrome`/`sameConfig` ask «is every key THIS
FILE states already stored with that value?» — a key the declaration drops is a key the comparison never
looks at, so deleting `middle_text` here would leave «Trocas e devoluções em até 30 dias» on an existing
box FOREVER and no birth would ever mention it. `""` is therefore an instruction and not a placeholder:
`wordOf` trims, so the area renders exactly as it would if the key were absent, and the difference is that
the seed now ASSERTS the absence. `seed/chrome.test.mjs` proves the omitted-key hole is real by driving
the plan over it.
⚠️ THE SHOE STORES SAID TWO WORDS FOR ONE THING, MEASURED: `seed/catalog.json` leaves `forge` and `outlet`
with an empty `vocabulary`, so their vitrine draws the kit's default — `Carrinho`
(packages/storefront-kit/src/vocabulary/vocabulary-keys.ts:52) — while this file wrote `Sacola` over the
account header of the same store. The café is the store that actually renamed the thing (`vocabulary.cart
= Sacola`) and is the one the owner told us to leave alone. So the instruction and the defect are the same
line, and the guard now ties the two files together instead of pinning a word.
⛔ STILL NO LOGO FOR `forge` AND `outlet`, AND NOW FOR A SECOND REASON. The first is unchanged: this
repository has no mark for them (`seed/photos/` holds `forge-co-logo.png` and its negative, and nothing
else that is a logo). The second is the component: `extensions/chrome/checkout-header.tsx:43-51` draws the
logo and the `back` word as ONE element — `{logo.url ? : back}` — so configuring a logo TODAY
would DELETE «Voltar à loja» from the funnel. The header the owner described (logo+step left, way back
right) needs three positions where the block has two; that is the monorepo's half of R4.

forge._why: The reference shoe store. TEXT ONLY, and the absence of a logo is a measurement rather than a shortcut: this tenant's asset library has no mark in it (04/09 — 18 582 catalogue photographs and seven banner tiles, no logo file anywhere in `seed/`), and pk19 added a second reason — the block draws `logo` and `back` as the same element, so a logo here would delete the way out of the funnel. The app's other road — a base word plus an accent-painted tail — is exactly the shape the theme's own wordmark has, so the store keeps a mark that reads like its own. ★ pk19: `cart` is `Carrinho` because that is what this store's VITRINE already says (empty `vocabulary` in seed/catalog.json ⇒ the kit's default); it said `Sacola` here, which made one store use two words for one thing.

outlet._why: The same brand under its own theme, and the mark is where that stops being a claim: `tail` is drawn in the theme's accent (carmine here, copper on the reference), so ONE placement makes the outlet look like the outlet without a line of code. ⚠️ pk19 TOOK THE SEAL OUT OF THE HEADER AND THE THREE INSTITUTIONAL SENTENCES OUT OF THE FOOTER: the owner called that content bad and dictated its replacement, and a store-specific promise («produtos originais com nota fiscal») is exactly the kind of claim he moved to one shared security line. The outlet keeps its own voice where he did not touch it — the way back and the footer's right-hand mark.

cafe._why: ★ THE STORE THIS ITEM WAS REALLY ABOUT. Its vitrine is a FORK and wears its own chrome; its CHECKOUT and its ACCOUNT screens are ours, hosted, and until this file they wore the reference mark — the café's buyers reached the payment step under somebody else's wordmark. This is the one entry with a LOGO, because it is the one store whose logo this repository actually has: `seed/photos/forge-co-logo.png`, the same mark the forked storefront imports as a bundled file (storefront-coffee/src/components/coffee/CoffeeChrome.tsx). The fork owns its copy; the hosted funnel needs it as an ASSET, which is what `logo` is — a `type:'id'` reference the kernel resolves to a url at read time. ★ pk19: the one store whose `cart` STAYS `Sacola` — the owner named it («na de café deixa como está») and the dataset agrees with him: `cafe` is the only store that declares `vocabulary.cart = Sacola` in seed/catalog.json, so here the account header and the vitrine already said the same word.

_balcao_why: ⛔ THE COUNTER GETS NO CHROME, AND IT IS NAMED HERE RATHER THAN SILENTLY SKIPPED — the same rule
`seed/box.json` writes for the warming step: «a store simply absent from a report is indistinguishable
from one that failed, and this repository has already paid twice for a summary that was silent about what
MEASURED: all five chrome blocks declare `surface: 'storefront'` and render inside the two deployables a
browser reaches — the vitrine (`brand`) and the hosted checkout/account screens (the other four). The
counter is neither. It is a whole-host app of its own (caddy `:82`, no store in the URL), it never appears
behind `/s/<id>` (`seed/box.json` marks it `servable: false` for exactly this reason) and it places its
orders through its own screens. Five placements there would render nowhere: rows in a Compose board that
an operator can move around and never see the effect of, which is a worse lesson than an empty board.
⇒ THE DEMO SHOWS THE APP IN THE THREE SHOPS A PERSON CAN OPEN. Wanting it on the counter as well is one
entry in `stores` above and no code change — that is what makes this a declaration rather than a decision
